pointers.sentence: The application has no models and no middleware, and `HumanizeConfig` names it and overrides nothing, `AppConfig.ready` included (`django/contrib/humanize/apps.py:HumanizeConfig`).

The `DjangoTemplates` backend finds the library in the application's templatetags package, so `{% load humanize %}` knows its name ([Libraries: `Library`, custom tags and `{% load %}`](../templates/libraries.md)); and the application's locale directory joins the catalogues `DjangoTranslation` merges, with the translations of the filters' words (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:DjangoTranslation._add_installed_apps_translations`) ([Message catalogues: `DjangoTranslation`](../i18n/catalogues.md)).
`is_safe=True` carries a safe input's safety to the result and creates none (`django/template/base.py:FilterExpression.resolve`) ([Autoescaping and safe strings](../templates/autoescape.md)).

The ordinal is marked safe so that, the comment there says, citing ticket 19988, a translation holding `"<sup>"` or `"<sub>"` is not broken (`django/contrib/humanize/templatetags/humanize.py:ordinal`).

`intcomma`, with its argument use_l10n true, the default, hands the value to `number_format` with `use_l10n=True` and `force_grouping=True`: the active language's separators, grouped whatever `USE_THOUSAND_SEPARATOR` says, unless the language's grouping is 0, as the default settings make it for one with no format module: Afrikaans got "45000" (`django/utils/formats.py:number_format`) ([Writing numbers, dates and durations](../i18n/writing-values.md)).

A value that cannot be made a decimal, and any value with the argument false, is written as its text, its leading digits grouped in threes by commas: the code's commas, in every language (`django/contrib/humanize/templatetags/humanize.py:intcomma`).

The count `ngettext` is given is `round_away_from_one` of the quotient, which rounds any number but 1.0 away from one, 1.2 to 2 and 0.5 to 0, so only a quotient of exactly 1.0 has the count 1; the documentation says this may be wrong for some languages (`django/utils/translation/__init__.py:round_away_from_one`, `docs/ref/contrib/humanize.txt`).

The count `ngettext` is given is `round_away_from_one` of the quotient, which rounds any number but 1.0 away from one, 1.2 to 2 and 0.5 to 0, so only a quotient of exactly 1.0 has the count 1; the documentation says this may be wrong for some languages (`django/utils/translation/__init__.py:round_away_from_one`, `docs/ref/contrib/humanize.txt`).

The quotient is rounded only as it is written, so 999,999,999 is "1000.0 million"; from a thousand decillions a number is counted in googols, and from a thousand googols it is given back (`django/contrib/humanize/templatetags/humanize.py:intword`).
`apnumber` writes 1 to 9 as words and gives back any other number (`django/contrib/humanize/templatetags/humanize.py:apnumber`).

It keeps the year, month and day, compares them with today, taken in the value's zone or, for a value without one, in local time, and gives "today", "tomorrow" or "yesterday"; any other day goes to the `|date` filter with the argument, or the active language's `DATE_FORMAT` (`django/contrib/humanize/templatetags/humanize.py:naturalday`).

A difference of a day or more goes to `django.utils.timesince.timesince`, or `timeuntil` for the future, which write up to two adjacent units, set in "%(delta)s ago" or "%(delta)s from now"; a smaller one is written in whole hours, minutes or seconds, the largest unit that fits, and less than a second is "now" (`django/contrib/humanize/templatetags/humanize.py:NaturalTimeFormatter.string_for`).

A count and its unit are joined by a non-breaking space, in the English phrases and, by `avoid_wrapping`, in timesince's units; translators' comments ask every language to keep it (`django/utils/html.py:avoid_wrapping`).

A `datetime.date` passes the filter's first test, the comment there noting that a datetime is a subclass of date, but `is_aware` then asks it for its offset from UTC, which a date lacks: `naturaltime` of today's date raised `AttributeError` out of the render (`django/utils/timezone.py:is_aware`).
